bull.b: Nkarta’s focus on off-the-shelf allogeneic NK cell therapies is a durable strategic edge: a scalable, standardized product reduces per-patient manufacturing complexity vs autologous approaches, supports broader commercial reach, and makes long-term partnerships and manufacturing scale more feasible.

Moderate debt-to-equity (~0.26 TTM) indicates the company is not overly reliant on borrowings, which lowers near-term insolvency risk and preserves flexibility to raise equity or debt when needed. This structural balance sheet profile supports continued R&D investment without heavy interest burden.

A multi-year reduction in net losses suggests improving cost discipline or operational efficiencies. Sustained improvement, if continued, can extend runway and reduce the magnitude of future financing needs, lowering long-term dilution risk and improving the prospect for advancing clinical programs.

bear.b: Consistent negative operating and free cash flow (~-$87M to -$88M TTM) is a structural weakness: it forces reliance on external funding, increases dilution risk, and can constrain the pace of clinical development or commercialization unless offset by revenue or substantial financings.

The absence of product revenue leaves the company dependent on pipeline progress and financing. This structurally limits visibility into long-term profitability, makes cash runway sensitive to trial outcomes, and raises execution risk until commercial sales are established.

Declining shareholders' equity and an historical reliance on equity financings indicate structural funding risk: future capital needs may dilute existing holders, and repeated raises can divert management focus, constrain long-term strategic choices, and pressure governance and financing terms.
